# Pre-Session {background-color="#2E4057"}

## Sleep & Lifestyle

Captured at session start — baseline state before activities

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}

| Variable | Type | Range |
|----------|------|-------|
| `sleep_hours` | Continuous | 0–14 hrs |
| `sleep_quality` | Ordinal | 1–5 |
| `caffeine_today` | Count | 0–10 cups |
| `exercise_week` | Count | 0–7 days |
| `screen_estimate` | Continuous | 0–16 hrs |

:::
::: {.column width="40%"}

**Why collect this?**

- Predictors of performance
- Correlation with mood
- Individual differences

:::
::::

## Mood PRE ⭐

Baseline measurement — enables pre-post comparison

| Variable | Type | Question | Range |
|----------|------|----------|-------|
| `mood_pre` | Ordinal | Current mood | 1 (negative) – 10 (positive) |
| `energy_pre` | Ordinal | Current energy | 1 (exhausted) – 10 (energetic) |
| `stress_pre` | Ordinal | Current stress | 1 (none) – 10 (extreme) |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Teaching Point
These match the POST measures — perfect for **paired t-tests** and **within-subjects** analysis
:::

# ⚡ Reflex Test {background-color="#2E4057"}

## Reflex Test — Variables

*How fast is your nervous system?*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Raw Data (recorded)**

| Variable | Type | Range |
|----------|------|-------|
| `rt_hand` | Categorical | Dom/Non-dom |
| `rt_trial1_cm` | Continuous | 0–30 cm |
| `rt_trial2_cm` | Continuous | 0–30 cm |
| `rt_trial3_cm` | Continuous | 0–30 cm |
| `rt_trial4_cm` | Continuous | 0–30 cm |
| `rt_trial5_cm` | Continuous | 0–30 cm |

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Calculated**

| Variable | Type | Range |
|----------|------|-------|
| `rt_trial[1-5]_ms` | Continuous | ~100–250 ms |
| `rt_mean_ms` | Continuous | ~120–220 ms |
| `rt_best_ms` | Continuous | ~100–180 ms |
| `rt_improvement` | Continuous | -50 to +80 ms |

:::
::::

## Reflex Test — Conversion

**Formula:** RT (ms) = √(2 × distance_m ÷ 9.81) × 1000

| Distance (cm) | RT (ms) | Distance (cm) | RT (ms) |
|---------------|---------|---------------|---------|
| 5 | 101 | 20 | 202 |
| 10 | 143 | 25 | 226 |
| 15 | 175 | 30 | 247 |

::: {.callout-note}
## Expected Distribution
**Right-skewed** — may need log transformation, median more appropriate than mean
:::

## Reflex Test — Teaching Points

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Statistical Tests**

- Paired t-test: Trial 1 vs Trial 5
- Correlation with sleep, caffeine
- Outlier detection (misses)

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Concepts**

- Practice effects
- Right-skewed distributions
- Log transformation
- Ratio scale measurement

:::
::::

# 🧠 Mind Palace {background-color="#2E4057"}

## Mind Palace — Variables

*What survives the interference?*

| Variable | Type | Description | Range |
|----------|------|-------------|-------|
| `mem_total` | Count | Words correctly recalled | 0–10 |
| `mem_pos1`...`mem_pos10` | Binary | Each position recalled? | Yes/No |
| `mem_intrusions` | Count | False memories | 0–10 |
| `mem_strategy` | Text | Strategy used | Open |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Between-Lab Manipulation
**Lab 304A:** Abstract words + Mozart (justice, freedom, beauty...)
**Lab 304B:** Concrete words + Silence (bicycle, mountain, umbrella...)
:::

## Mind Palace — Teaching Points

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Statistical Tests**

- Independent t-test: concrete vs abstract
- Serial position analysis
- Chi-square: position × recalled

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Concepts**

- Imageability effect
- Primacy/recency effects
- False memories (intrusions)
- Ceiling effects

:::
::::

# ⏰ Time Warp {background-color="#2E4057"}

## Time Warp — Variables

*Your brain's internal clock*

| Variable | Type | Description | Range |
|----------|------|-------------|-------|
| `time_estimate_sec` | Continuous | 60-sec estimation | ~30–90 sec |
| `time_error` | Continuous | Estimate − 60 | -30 to +30 |
| `line1_estimate_cm` | Continuous | Line 1 estimate (visual) | 1–25 cm |
| `line2_estimate_cm` | Continuous | Line 2 estimate (visual) | 1–25 cm |
| `string1_estimate_cm` | Continuous | String 1 estimate (tactile) | 1–40 cm |
| `string2_estimate_cm` | Continuous | String 2 estimate (tactile) | 1–40 cm |
| `temp_estimate_c` | Continuous | Room temp guess | 15–30 °C |
| `time_counting` | Categorical | Counted during? | Yes steady/Yes sometimes/No |
| `music_condition` | Categorical | Condition (by lab) | silence/music |

## Time Warp — Teaching Points

::: {.callout-warning}
## Between-Lab Manipulation
**Lab 304A:** 60-second estimation with background music (Mozart)
**Lab 304B:** 60-second estimation in silence
:::

**Statistical Tests**

- One-sample t-test: Is mean time_error ≠ 0?
- Independent t-test: Silence vs music
- Systematic bias analysis

**Concepts**

- Normally distributed errors
- Internal clock
- Effect of distraction

# 👁️ Sixth Sense {background-color="#2E4057"}

## Sixth Sense — Variables

*Can you feel the gaze?*

**Trial-level (×6 trials)**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `stare_t[1-6]_actual` | Binary | Actually staring? |
| `stare_t[1-6]_guess` | Binary | Participant's guess |
| `stare_t[1-6]_conf` | Ordinal | Confidence (1–5) |

**Summary (calculated)**

| Variable | Type | Description | Range |
|----------|------|-------------|-------|
| `stare_correct_total` | Count | Correct detections | 0–6 |
| `stare_hit_rate` | Proportion | P(detect | staring) | 0–1 |
| `stare_fa_rate` | Proportion | P(detect | not staring) | 0–1 |

## Sixth Sense — Teaching Points

::: {.callout-note}
## The Null Hypothesis
If staring cannot be detected, accuracy should be **50%** (about 3/6 correct)
:::

**Statistical Tests**

- Binomial test: accuracy vs 50%
- Signal detection: d' from hits & false alarms
- Confidence calibration

**Concepts**

- Chance performance
- Binomial distribution
- Type I and Type II errors

# 🎲 Lady Luck {background-color="#2E4057"}

## Lady Luck — Random Numbers

*Are you truly random?*

**Self-generated numbers (1–10)**

| Variable | Type | Description | Range |
|----------|------|-------------|-------|
| `rand_num1`...`rand_num20` | Discrete | Each "random" number | 1–10 |
| `rand_mean` | Continuous | Mean of 20 numbers | 1–10 |
| `rand_repeats` | Count | Adjacent repeats | 0–19 |
| `rand_mode` | Discrete | Most frequent number | 1–10 |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Human Randomness Bias
People avoid repeats, favour certain numbers (7!), and alternate too much.
True random mean should be **5.5**
:::

## Lady Luck — Dice & Coins

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Dice (10 rolls)**

| Variable | Type | Range |
|----------|------|-------|
| `dice_roll1`...`dice_roll10` | Discrete | 1–6 |
| `dice_sixes` | Count | 0–10 |
| `dice_predict` | Categorical | Yes/No/Unsure |

Expected 6s: **~1.67**

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Coins (10 flips)**

| Variable | Type | Range |
|----------|------|-------|
| `coin_flip1`...`coin_flip10` | Binary | H/T |
| `coin_heads` | Count | 0–10 |
| `coin_longest_run` | Count | 1–10 |

Expected heads: **5**

:::
::::

## Lady Luck — Teaching Points

**Statistical Tests**

- Chi-square goodness of fit (dice → uniform?)
- Binomial test (coin heads vs expected)
- Runs test for randomness

**Concepts**

- Uniform distribution
- Binomial distribution
- Human inability to generate randomness
- Gambler's fallacy

| Variable | Type | Description | Range |

**Concepts**

- Overconfidence bias
- Dunning-Kruger effect

# Post-Session {background-color="#2E4057"}

## Mood POST ⭐

Endpoint measurement — matches PRE for paired comparison

| Variable | Type | Question | Range |
|----------|------|----------|-------|
| `mood_post` | Ordinal | Current mood | 1–10 |
| `energy_post` | Ordinal | Current energy | 1–10 |
| `stress_post` | Ordinal | Current stress | 1–10 |

**Change Scores (calculated)**

| Variable | Formula | Interpretation |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `mood_change` | post − pre | Positive = improved |
| `energy_change` | post − pre | Positive = more energy |
| `stress_change` | post − pre | Negative = less stressed |

## Pre-Post Analysis

::: {.callout-tip}
## The Big Question
Did participating in DataLab affect your mood?
:::

**Paired t-test:** Is mean `mood_change` significantly different from 0?

**Further questions:**

- Does extraversion predict mood improvement?
- Does baseline stress predict stress reduction?
- Regression to the mean?

## Session Feedback

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `enjoyed_overall` | Ordinal (1–10) | Overall enjoyment |
| `fav_station` | Categorical (1–6) | Favourite experiment |
| `least_fav_station` | Categorical (1–6) | Least favourite |

**Analysis ideas:**

- Bar chart: Which station was most popular?
- Correlation: enjoyment vs mood_change
- Group differences in preferences

# Summary {background-color="#2E4057"}

## What We Collected

| Section | Variables | Key Analysis |
|---------|-----------|--------------|
| Pre-session | 11 | Baseline predictors |
| ⚡ Reflex Test | 9 | Practice effects, RT distribution |
| 🧠 Mind Palace | 14 | Concrete vs abstract (between-lab) |
| ⏰ Time Warp | 9 | Silence vs music (between-lab) |
| 👁️ Sixth Sense | 21 | Binomial test vs 50% |
| 🎲 Lady Luck | 35+ | Chi-square, human randomness |
| 🎯 Frontal Lob | 7 | 2m vs 3m (between-lab), calibration |
| Post-session | 9 | Pre-post mood change |

**Total: ~115 variables per participant**

## Your Data Journey

Over the coming weeks, you'll analyse this dataset to:

1. Test hypotheses with **t-tests** and **chi-square**
2. Explore relationships with **correlation** and **regression**
3. Compare distributions (normal, skewed, binomial, uniform)
4. Understand **within-subjects** vs **between-subjects** designs
5. Calculate **effect sizes** and interpret **p-values**

::: {.callout-note}
## Remember
This is *your* data — collected by you, about you. Every analysis tells a story about human psychology.
:::
